tasks.short: Write and review specs for Power BI reports and AFAS extracts: definitions, sources, DAX logic, access rules.

today.trigger: An HR Business Partner, the HR Director or Finance asks for a new or changed report or dashboard, or an AFAS change breaks an existing one.
steps: Collect the request by Teams or mail and pin down which question the report has to answer
Look up the AFAS fields, extract views and existing Power BI model to find sources
Write a spec in Word on SharePoint: metric definitions, filters, DAX measures, row-level security, refresh
Review the spec with the requester and, where personal data is involved, check it against the privacy register
Update the documentation after the build and when definitions change
drudgery: Copying field lists and table descriptions from AFAS and the Power BI model by hand
Rewriting the same definitions (FTE, verzuim rate, 90-day retention) in every spec
Keeping documentation in step with the model after small changes
today.time_sinks: Reverse-engineering what an existing measure actually does and chasing requesters for agreement on definitions.

lenses.faster: Copilot reads the Power BI model and AFAS extract schema and drafts the spec, field list and DAX explanations; the analyst edits instead of writing from scratch.
lenses.autonomous: When the semantic model changes in the nightly refresh pipeline, a job regenerates the data dictionary and flags measures whose documentation no longer matches.
lenses.ambitious: Every HR metric gets one documented definition with owner, source, privacy basis and minimum group size, which is the base a manager Q&A agent needs.
lenses.joy: No more retyping field lists or decoding old DAX; the analyst spends the time agreeing definitions with HR and Finance.
lenses.options: Draft two or three design options per request (extend existing model, new page, paginated report) with effort and privacy impact side by side.
lenses.altitude: The analyst stops writing specs one by one and owns a metric layer template and review checklist that AI-drafted specs must pass.
reach: Draft the processing description for the privacy officer and the works council consent request for a new HR report
Document Finance's AFAS general ledger extract definitions with the Controller and FP&A Analysts

tasks.human_edge: Agreeing what a metric means with HR and Finance, judging what a works council or privacy officer will accept, and spotting where the source data does not support the request.
tasks.pattern_why: Input is a loose request plus a known model; the draft is quick for AI but definitions, privacy choices and sign-off need the analyst.

in_practice.trigger: New report request logged in the HR request list, or a schema change detected in the Power BI model.
steps: Analyst pastes the request; copilot pulls model metadata (tables, measures, RLS roles) and the metric glossary
Copilot drafts spec: purpose, definitions, sources, DAX, access, refresh, privacy notes
Analyst corrects definitions and design choices and reviews with the requester
Approved spec saved to SharePoint; data dictionary regenerated from the model after build
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst signs off every spec; requester confirms definitions; anything touching personal or health data is checked against the privacy register and OR consent.
data_needed: Privacy register and OR consent scope
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint spec library with version history

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI writes DAX and summarises reports on a semantic model, but can misinterpret data without a prepared model.
evidence.source: Microsoft Learn, Copilot in Power BI [S5]

evidence.claim: Text-to-SQL cut query authoring from about 10 to 3 minutes, but hallucinated tables and columns remain.
LLMs can draft spec documents and data dictionaries from schema metadata.

risks: Draft invents fields or measures that do not exist in the AFAS extract
Definitions drift if the glossary is not maintained
Copilot in Power BI needs Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity, which Noordhaven may not have
Dutch-language prompts are not officially supported
research_questions: Does Noordhaven's Power BI tenant have Fabric or Premium capacity for Copilot?
How many specs per year are written, and how long does each take today?
Does a drafted spec from model metadata need less than half the editing time of a hand-written one on three real requests?

tasks.short: Keep track of HR tech and analytics trends and vendors to advise what Noordhaven should adopt next.

today.trigger: A vendor pitch, a question from the HR Director, an AFAS or Microsoft release, or budget planning.
steps: Read newsletters, vendor blogs, AFAS and Microsoft release notes and LinkedIn posts
Attend webinars and talk with peers at other logistics firms
Compare options (Power BI Copilot, Visier, Recruitee and Studytube features) against Noordhaven needs
Write a short note or slides for the HR Director with a recommendation
drudgery: Wading through vendor marketing to find what a product actually does
Re-checking release notes for features that are not in the Dutch or EU offering
today.time_sinks: Reading volume and separating vendor claims from evidence.

lenses.faster: A monthly scan summarises releases and articles with sources, the claim, the evidence grade and the caveat; the analyst reads one page instead of thirty.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled job watches AFAS, Microsoft, Recruitee and Studytube release notes and flags items that touch Noordhaven's stack.
lenses.ambitious: Every vendor pitch gets an evidence check (named customer, measured result, EU AI Act and works council impact) before anyone books a demo.
lenses.joy: Less skimming of marketing pages; more time testing the two or three tools that matter.
lenses.options: For a need such as manager Q&A, compare build on Power BI, buy Visier, or wait, with cost and risk per scenario.
lenses.altitude: The analyst runs a small evidence register of HR tech claims and a decision rule for when a trend is worth a pilot.
reach: Prepare vendor shortlists and requirements for the HR Director and procurement
Brief the works council on new HR tools and their consent implications

tasks.human_edge: Judging fit with Noordhaven's shift workforce, CAO and works council, and talking to peers and vendors in person.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured articles and release notes turn into a structured, sourced summary inside a scheduled scan; the analyst checks before it goes to the HR Director.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly schedule, plus ad hoc when a vendor pitch or management question arrives.
steps: Fetch release notes and a fixed source list
LLM extracts claim, product, evidence grade, source link and caveat per item
Filter to items that touch AFAS, Power BI, Recruitee, Studytube or Dutch/EU rules
Analyst reviews, adds judgment and sends a one-page brief
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst verifies sources and any recommendation before it reaches the HR Director; vendor contacts stay with the analyst.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or an LLM API
data_needed: Source list (vendor release notes, regulators, trade press)
Noordhaven stack and open needs list
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint evidence register (list) with dates and sources

evidence.claim: Vendor HR agents are sold (Microsoft Workforce Insights, Visier Vee, Workday MCP access) without published customer results.
Vendor and trend reports often overstate; 48% of employees exaggerated AI use, and Workday's report cannot establish AI's causal role.
LLMs summarise articles into structured, sourced notes reliably enough for a reviewed brief.

risks: Summaries repeat vendor claims without the caveat
Invented sources or links if not checked
Most trend material is US-centric and misses Dutch works council and AVG constraints
research_questions: Does the HR Director act on the monthly brief, or is the task mainly ad hoc pitch checks?
What share of summarised items survive the analyst's source check unchanged over three months?
Which sources cover Dutch HR tech and works council decisions well enough to include?

role.altitude: From producing reports and specs to owning Noordhaven's HR metric layer: definitions, verified answers, access rules, privacy checks and data quality checks that managers and agents query.
reach: Answering routine manager questions on headcount, verzuim and flex use now handled by HR Business Partners
Preparing works council and privacy documentation for HR data processing
Supporting FP&A with labour cost and flex worker spend analysis from AFAS and agency invoices
Vendor evaluation for HR tools with the HR Director
role.ceiling_note: Limited by AFAS data quality, Power BI capacity licensing, works council consent for anything that can observe performance, GDPR Art. 9 on absence data, and from Dec 2027 EU AI Act high-risk duties; the role is 1 FTE, so time freed is a few hundred hours a year at most.
skills_to_grow: Semantic model and metric glossary design in Power BI
Prompting and evaluating Copilot and LLM output against known answers
Privacy by design, WOR article 27 and EU AI Act basics
Python for data quality checks and automation
Writing verified answers and test sets for manager Q&A
role.ambitious_version: Every manager at three sites gets correct answers on hiring, 90-day retention, verzuim and flex use in Teams within seconds, with row-level security and minimum group sizes, while the analyst spends most of the time on definitions, checks and deeper questions such as why 90-day retention differs by site.
